# LazyProf

[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/badge/CurseForge-LazyProf-orange)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/lazyprof)
[![Wago](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wago-LazyProf-c1272d)](https://addons.wago.io/addons/lazyprof)
[![License: All Rights Reserved](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-All_Rights_Reserved-red.svg)](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![PayPal](https://img.shields.io/badge/Donate-PayPal-00457C?logo=paypal&logoColor=white)](https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=FG4KES3HNPLVG)
[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy_Me_A_Coffee-FFDD00?logo=buy-me-a-coffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/kaldown)

If you find this useful, consider supporting development via [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=FG4KES3HNPLVG) or [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/kaldown).

Other addons:
- [VendorSniper](https://addons.wago.io/addons/vendorsniper) - Vendor restock sniper
- [Silencer](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/silencer-whispers) - Whisper gatekeeper
- [CraftLib](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/craftlib) - Recipe database
- [PickMe](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/pickme) - LFG listing browser
- [EyesOnMe](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/eyesonme) - PvP targeting awareness

Calculate the cheapest path to level your professions in World of Warcraft.

**Requires [CraftLib](https://github.com/kaldown/CraftLib)** - Install both addons together.

## Supported Professions

See [CraftLib's profession coverage](https://github.com/kaldown/CraftLib#profession-coverage) for the current list of supported professions.

## Features

- **Plan, then shop** - Open a profession and see the cheapest path from your real skill, counting what you already own, current prices and what the crafted items sell for. Choose how far to level and get one total of what to buy
- **One window: Crafts and Shopping** - A window beside the profession window with two tabs under a shared header. The header answers how far ("Level to") and what it costs (the receipt); Crafts lists what you will craft, in order; Shopping says what to collect and what to buy
- **Level to** - A number box and a slider from your skill to the last cap. Drag the slider, or type a skill and press Enter: the path, the costs and the shopping list end there. To shop for the next bracket only, set it to that bracket's end
- **The receipt** - "You spend" (reagents still to buy plus recipes to buy or learn), "Back from selling" (what the crafts sell for) and "Net cost". Amounts are exact to the copper, and "You spend" is the Shopping tab added up. Further lines say what your own stock saves and what making reagents yourself saves or costs
- **Sale value** - What the crafted items sell for is counted: sold to a vendor by default, at auction after the 5% cut, or not at all. Under Cheapest, two recipes that need the same reagents are no longer equal when one sells for more
- **Your stock shapes the path** - Under Cheapest, reagents you own are counted when the path is chosen, against whole runs of a recipe. The planner compares up to four routes and keeps the one you pay least for, so the path never costs you more than the market-price path would, by the addon's own count
- **The plan you shopped for stays** - Under Cheapest the route is remembered per character and profession, so after buying the list the path does not wander to other recipes. It gives way when it would cost more than the market-price path or another route is clearly cheaper; choosing a recipe yourself plans that range again
- **Crafts tab** - The plan as a numbered list of crafts in the order you make them ("1  7x Wild Leather Leggings", skill range, cost), with what each craft uses on the line under it: green for what you have, "(buy 14)" for what you still need, "(from 1)" for what an earlier craft makes. What has to be learned first is a line under its recipe, training the next rank is a row of its own, and the closest alternative is offered right under a craft with a Use button. Nothing is opened until you click a craft: then its reagents with their cost, what a craft sells for, how to learn the recipe and the other recipes for that skill range
- **Alternative recipes** - "Use" swaps the recipe over that skill range and plans again at once; "Reset" gives the choice back to the planner. Your choices are kept between sessions
- **Two strategies** - Cheapest (minimize gold) or Fastest (minimize crafts)
- **Spare crafts** - Plan extra crafts and reagents for bad luck with skill-ups (5 to 30 percent, 15 by default)
- **More options** - One switch in the window shows the rest: Cheapest / Fastest, "Spare crafts", the selling mode, where the prices come from, the recipe search, "Hide what I have" and the craft-or-buy buttons
- **Need / Have / Buy** - The shopping list is one table per reagent: what is still to buy first, the dearest on top, then what you make yourself, then what you already own. What is in your bags is taken off (on WoW Forever the reagent bag too), and with Syndicator also what is in your bank, mail, auctions and on alts (the guild bank if you turn it on). Without Syndicator the Shopping tab says that only your bags are counted. Vendor-sold reagents carry a "vendor" mark, every reagent says which craft it is for ("for 2. Blue Suede Shoes"), and the recipes still to buy or learn are listed with their price
- **Craft or buy per reagent** - LazyProf crafts intermediates (e.g., smelt ore into bars) when that is cheaper; under More options you can choose "I craft it" or "I buy it" per item instead
- **Buy vendor reagents in one click** - At a merchant that sells reagents on your list, a small panel offers a Buy button per reagent and "Buy all" with the total on the button. Limited-stock items and items not sold for gold are listed but never bought automatically
- **Skill gaps** - Paths bridge a gap with a green recipe while its skill-up chance is at least 10%, otherwise the gap is shown
- **Recipe Availability Filtering** - Only suggests recipes you can actually obtain - checks inventory, trainers, vendors, and Auction House listings
- **Recipe details panel** - View ingredients, difficulty thresholds, sources, and Wowhead links
- **Planning mode** - The same window, opened from the minimap button or `/lp browse`, plans any profession without opening it - or without having learned it
- **Every Classic expansion** - One install plans correctly on Classic Era / Vanilla, Season of Discovery, The Burning Crusade, and Wrath of the Lich King (including Inscription, skill cap 450) - it detects your client and uses the right recipes, caps, racial bonuses, and Wowhead links automatically
- **WoW Forever** - Runs on WoW Forever 1.60 from the same install, with native frames, tabs and dropdowns and an addon compartment entry instead of a minimap button. On Forever LazyProf also remembers the profession trainers you visit and the fees they charge, and names them where a recipe is still to learn or the next rank is to train. Forever recipe data covers all nine professions: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Leatherworking, Tailoring, Cooking, First Aid and Mining (smelting). No race has a profession bonus on Forever, so none is applied there. Known limits: required tools are not used for paths yet, and the skill cap is assumed to be 300 until confirmed

## Pricing

**Vendor prices always come first** - reagents sold by NPCs (dyes, threads, vials, flux, etc.) use their fixed vendor price: from TSM or Auctionator's recorded merchant data, from merchants you have visited with LazyProf installed (it remembers what they sell for gold without a stock limit), or from the built-in vendor list. This prevents AH markup from inflating recipe costs.

For non-vendor items, market sources are checked in order:
1. **TSM** - Configurable pricing (Recent, MinBuyout, Market, or Regional)
2. **Auctionator** - Auctionator scan prices

An Auctionator price from a scan you made this session (since login or /reload) is used before TSM, because it is newer than the TSM data loaded at login. A reagent no source can price is estimated from its vendor sell value.

**What crafts sell for** - Sold to a vendor, a crafted item counts at the vendor's price the game reports for it. Sold at auction, it counts at its TSM or Auctionator price after the 5% cut, never less than the vendor's price. One item per craft is assumed.

**Recommended:** Install [TSM](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/tradeskill-master) + TSM Desktop App for the most accurate pricing.

## Optional Dependencies

| Addon | Feature |
|-------|---------|
| [TradeSkillMaster](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/tradeskill-master) | TSM pricing integration |
| [Auctionator](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/auctionator) | Auctionator pricing + shift-click search |
| [Syndicator](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/syndicator) | Stock outside your bags: bank, mail, your auctions, alts, guild bank |

## Usage

1. **Open any profession window** - The LazyProf window opens beside it, and an arrow marks the next recipe in the profession's list
2. **Choose how far to level** - Drag the "Level to" slider, or type a skill and press Enter. The receipt under it says what that costs
3. **Shop** - The Shopping tab lists what to collect first (bank, mail, alts - with Syndicator) and what to buy
4. **Come back and craft** - The Crafts tab marks the craft you are on and moves on by itself as your skill goes up
5. **Minimap button** (addon compartment on WoW Forever) - Plan any profession without opening it
   - Left-click: Open profession browser
   - Right-click: Open settings
6. **At a vendor** - If the vendor sells reagents on your list, the LazyProf panel next to the merchant window buys them

The merchant panel uses the shopping list of the path you last looked at in this play session, so open the profession (or the LazyProf window) once before shopping.

Commands:
- `/lazyprof` or `/lp` - Open settings
- `/lp browse` - Open profession browser
- `/lp resetpanels` - Move the window and panels back to their default place and size
- `/lp log` - Open debug log window
- `/lp diag` - List the diagnostic dumps (prices, merchant, trainer, stock, client)

## Settings

Access via `/lp` or the Interface Options panel:

- **Strategy** - Cheapest (minimize gold) or Fastest (minimize crafts); also in the window, under More options
- **Count what crafts sell for** - Sold to a vendor (default), sold at auction after the 5% cut, or do not count; also "Selling" in the window, under More options
- **Spare crafts (percent)** - How many extra crafts "Spare crafts" plans per step (5-30, default 15)
- **Material Resolution** - What reagents without a choice of their own do: never craft intermediates, craft when cheaper, or always craft
- **Suggest unlearned recipes** - Include recipes you haven't learned yet
- **Open with the profession window** - Show the LazyProf window whenever you open a profession (on by default)
- **Include bank items** - Count what is in your bank as owned, for the path and the shopping list (on by default; requires Syndicator)
- **Include alt characters** - Count materials on all your characters as owned (on by default; requires Syndicator)
- **Include guild bank** - Count guild bank materials as owned (off by default; requires Syndicator)
- **Include recipes bought with currency** - Suggest recipes sold for a currency (such as Merchant's Favor) even before you learn them (off by default)
- **Reset panel positions** - Move the window and panels back to their default place and size (also `/lp resetpanels`)

Without Syndicator the three stock options are greyed out and only the bags of the character you play are counted; with bank or alts switched on, the Shopping tab says so in its first line.

A character in Self-Found mode cannot be sent anything: no stock of your other characters or of the guild bank is counted for it. A character the game itself marks Self-Found is treated the same for stock, also with the setting off.

The target skill, the recipes you chose, the route you follow, craft-or-buy choices and the last tab you used are remembered per character.

## Supported Game Versions

One install works on every live Classic-family client - it detects which one you are on (via CraftLib) and plans with the correct recipes and skill cap:

- Classic Era / Anniversary (Vanilla) - cap 300
- Season of Discovery - cap 300
- The Burning Crusade Classic - cap 375
- Wrath of the Lich King Classic - cap 450, includes Inscription (also loads on the Titan 3.80 seasonal client)
- Hardcore (Classic Era)
- WoW Forever 1.60 - cap 300 (assumed until confirmed); all 9 professions

# LazyProf

## [v0.12.1](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/tree/v0.12.1) (2026-11-27)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/compare/v0.12.0...v0.12.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/releases)

- docs: release v0.12.1  
- Merge branch 'fix/crafts-followups'  
- fix(ui): draw icons that arrive during a recipe search  
    A craft whose icon data arrived while a recipe search was shown kept  
    its question mark after the search was cleared: the window now redraws  
    for it during the search too. The tooltip of a craft whose made  
    reagent has no price to buy it only says where that reagent's own  
    reagents are listed, which holds even when they have no price either.  
- docs: describe how Cheapest ranks recipes that pay for themselves  
    The decision record, the component notes and the changelog say what  
    changed: recipes that cost nothing rank by what one craft leaves,  
    crafted-item icons are drawn once their data arrives, and the craft  
    line names a made reagent without a price to buy it.  
- fix(pathfinder): rank recipes that pay for themselves by what a craft leaves  
    Under Cheapest a recipe's cost after what its craft sells for stops at  
    zero, so every recipe that pays for itself scored the same and the  
    tie went to the one with the better skill-up chance. On WoW Forever  
    Leatherworking 250-255 with the leather owned, that chose Blue Suede  
    Shoes (bought thread and dye, sold for 96s 65c) over Wild Leather  
    Leggings (owned leather, sold for 1g 15s 85c), several gold dearer.  
    Recipes that cost nothing now come first, ordered by what one craft  
    leaves the player, then as before. Among them the order is counted  
    per craft, with a recipe's fee spread over the skill points left, so  
    a lower chance never moves one of them ahead of another. Scores are  
    unchanged and never negative, and paths planned without sale values  
    are the same as before.  
- fix(ui): draw crafted-item icons once their data arrives  
    A craft whose crafted item had not been loaded yet showed a question  
    mark, and with Selling set to "Do not count" nothing drew the window  
    again when the item's data came. The window now says which of its  
    crafts wait for an icon, and the arrival of that data redraws it once,  
    batched like the planning that follows item data, without planning  
    again.  
- test(views): check the uses line on bundled Forever Tailoring data  
    Tailoring 1-150 makes Bolts of Mageweave in one craft and uses them in  
    the Tuxedo Pants later: the pants' line says "(from N, buy 5)" with  
    the number of the craft that made them, and the Shopping tab buys only  
    those 5.  
- fix(views): say when a reagent you make has no price to buy it  
    With "I craft it" on a reagent that has no price to buy it, the  
    craft's cost showed a question mark while its uses line said only  
    "(make N)", and the summary claimed that making it cost more than  
    buying it, with nothing to compare against. The uses line now says  
    "(make N, no buy price)" in orange, the craft's tooltip says why its  
    cost is unknown and that the Shopping tab counts what making it  
    costs, and the summary makes no claim about making while a made  
    reagent has no price to buy it.  
- test(views): check every colour helper for a pipe in its text  
    The static check looked at Grey and Green only; White and Orange are  
    checked too, and the check proves it catches a planted pipe for each.  
    The tabs widget's usage note names the tabs as they are now.  
- fix(ui): start a craft's icon where its number column ends  
    The number column ended at 22 and the icon started at 20, so the two  
    overlapped by 2 pixels. The icon now starts at 22 and the name at 40,  
    with or without an icon; the lines under a craft move with the name.  
    The layout check also looks at the number and the icon.

# LazyProf

## [v0.12.0](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/tree/v0.12.0) (2026-11-27)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/compare/v0.11.0...v0.12.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/releases)

- docs: release v0.12.0  
- chore: update CraftLib submodule  
- Merge branch 'fix/diag-spec-wording'  
- fix(diag): say what an item with no data means in /lp diag spec  
    An item the client has no data for was reported as "run /lp diag spec  
    again", which helps nothing when the game does not serve the item at all.  
    The line now says the data was asked for, and one note at the end says  
    that an item still without data on a second run is not in the game now.  
- Merge branch 'docs/spec-ingame-s1'  
- docs(client): note that IsSpellKnown answers for specialization passives  
- Merge branch 'feat/specialization'  
- feat(diag): say when the client knows no such teaching item  
    /lp diag spec tells a pattern whose data is still on its way from one the  
    client does not have. The changelog and the troubleshooting guide cover  
    trainer recipes judged by the item they make.  
- fix(pathfinder): a pin of a recipe left out for its specialization cuts no run  
    Trainer recipes that need a specialization now leave the TBC paths too  
    (Golden Dragonstrike Breastplate, Living Crystal Breastplate, Gnomish  
    Poultryizer in the snapshots); a pin or remembered range naming such a  
    recipe no longer splits the run around it.  
- chore: update CraftLib submodule  
    Trainer recipes that need a specialization now carry it too.  
- docs: describe the specialization fix  
- feat(diag): /lp diag spec  
    Lists, per profession, the specializations the character knows, how many  
    recipes each one leaves out, and for each recipe whose pattern has no entry in the game  
    data (so what it requires is not known), its tooltip as the client shows it.  
- fix(pathfinder): leave out recipes that need a specialization the character lacks  
    A recipe whose pattern needs a profession specialization the character  
    does not know (Chimeric Boots needs Tribal Leatherworking) is no longer a  
    candidate: it is never chosen, never listed as an alternative, and a pin  
    or remembered route naming it falls back to another recipe. A pattern of  
    that kind in the bags no longer counts, Self-Found mode cannot bring it  
    back, and craft-or-buy does not assume it was learned. With no  
    specialization known, every recipe that needs one is left out, and so is  
    one whose requirement the game data cannot tell. Recipes already learned  
    stay usable.  
- feat(client): ask the client which spells the character knows  
    Client:KnowsSpell(spellId) answers through C\_SpellBook.IsSpellKnown on WoW  
    Forever and IsPlayerSpell / IsSpellKnown on the other clients;  
    Client:ItemTooltipText(itemId) reads an item's tooltip lines on WoW Forever.  
    Self-Found's smelting check goes through the adapter, and the spell and  
    tooltip calls are now forbidden outside it.  
- chore: update CraftLib submodule  
    Recipes that need a profession specialization now carry it.  
- Merge branch 'feat/craft-plan'  
- fix(ui): say once why the arrow cannot point at a recipe split by a rank step  
- docs: describe the Crafts tab and the shopping notes  
- feat(ui): each shopping row names the craft it is for  
- feat(ui): Crafts tab - numbered crafts with what each one uses  
- feat(ui): crafts column layout and a number column for list rows  
- feat(guide): record which run made a reagent and each run's icon

# LazyProf

## [v0.11.0](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/tree/v0.11.0) (2026-11-25)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/compare/v0.10.1...v0.11.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/releases)

- docs: release v0.11.0  
- Merge branch 'fix/syndicator-alts'  
- fix(inventory): count Syndicator alts of the same realm and faction only  
    Every character Syndicator knew counted as an alt, of every realm and  
    faction, soulbound items included, so the shopping list could rely on  
    stock the character can never be sent. An alt now counts only when  
    Syndicator records the same realm and faction for it as for the  
    character being played, and its bound items (isBound) are left out;  
    the character's own bound items still count. A character Syndicator has  
    no realm or faction for does not count.  
    /lp diag stock says which alts count and why the others do not, and  
    shows the fields of one stored item, so the bound mark can be checked.  
- Merge branch 'fix/window-minor'  
- fix(settings): name everything a reset clears  
    A reset wipes the whole saved database, but its question and message  
    named only the vendor prices, trainers, targets and craft-or-buy  
    choices. They now also name the chosen recipes, remembered routes,  
    Self-Found mode, window positions and the known recipes, which are read  
    again when each profession is opened.  
- fix(ui): say on the status line when the path is the fastest one  
    The Cheapest / Fastest buttons now sit under More options, so a player  
    whose saved strategy is Fastest saw a dearer path with no hint why. The  
    status line ends with "fastest path" while that strategy is in force.  
- fix(ui): redraw the window when it shows after a redraw it missed  
    A stock change during combat (or the end of the wait for sale values)  
    asked for a redraw while combat had the window hidden; the redraw was  
    skipped, and showing the window again only laid out the old view, so  
    the receipt and the Shopping tab kept the counts from before combat  
    until the next change. A skipped redraw is now done when the window  
    shows again.  
- fix(ui): commit an unheard slider release to the path it was made on  
    When the mouse was let go outside the window, the release was found at  
    the next redraw. If that redraw came with another profession's path,  
    the dragged target was stored on the new profession. The window now  
    asks the slider before it takes a new path.  
- Merge branch 'shop/syndicator-stock'  
- Merge branch 'docs/sale-age-note'  
- docs: describe the auction price age rule with the sale value entry  
- Merge branch 'fix/stale-sale-price'  
- fix(pricing): do not count an old auction price as what a craft sells for  
    In the auction selling mode the sale value took the market price of the  
    crafted item whatever its age, and nothing warned about it: the price  
    warnings cover the path's reagents only. A market price now comes with  
    its age when the source knows it, and one PRICE\_STALE\_DAYS or more old  
    is not counted for a sale; the vendor value counts instead.  
- docs: bank and alts come from Syndicator; the own stock memory is withdrawn  
    ADR-019 records why the memory was taken out before any release, and  
    ADR-018 is marked as superseded by it. The changelog's unreleased  
    section drops the memory entries and says that bank and alt stock are  
    counted through Syndicator, with the bags only and a line on the  
    Shopping tab without it. README, description, the architecture notes,  
    the testing guide and the /lp diag stock section of the troubleshooting  
    guide say the same.  
- Merge branch 'fix/choice-right-click'  
- fix(ui): let right-click put a craft or buy choice back to automatic  
    The row button uses the stock button template, which takes left clicks  
    only, so the right-click its tooltip promised never arrived. A row  
    button now registers right clicks when its descriptor asks for them,  
    and the craft / buy button does. A choice the player made also keeps  
    its button without More options: it still changes the list there, and  
    nothing showed it or could undo it.  
- feat(inventory): list the characters Syndicator knows in /lp diag stock  
    One line per name of Syndicator.API.GetAllCharacters(): the full name,  
    whether it is the character played, and every plain value (text,  
    number, true/false) of its record's details, sorted by key; at most 60  
    characters, then how many more. Every call and table is read  
    defensively, so a missing field or a failing call is said in the line  
    and never raised.  
    On WoW Forever the realm name is a shard name that can change: the  
    block shows whether Syndicator keeps the same character twice under  
    two realm names.  
- feat(settings): drop the saved bag and bank memory of an unreleased build  
    MigrateSettings now removes LazyProfDB.global.stock at load. Only an  
    unreleased build wrote it; bank and alt stock come from the Syndicator  
    addon, and nothing writes the table any more.  
- Merge branch 'fix/receipt-note-wrap'  
- fix(ui): put a receipt note that does not fit on its own line  
    At the default width the note of "You spend" (reagents ... + recipes  
    ...) wrapped inside its last amount, leaving "85c" alone on the next  
    line. A note wider than the room beside its amount now goes whole on  
    its own line under its label; it wraps only when the window is too  
    narrow even for that.  
- feat(ui): say on the Shopping tab when only the bags are counted  
    Without the Syndicator addon only the carried bags of the character  
    count. When "Include bank items" or "Include alt characters" is on, the  
    Shopping tab now opens with one grey line: "Only the bags of this  
    character are counted. Install Syndicator to count your bank and alts  
    too." It comes from the stock scan (meta.bagsOnly) and is built in the  
    views as data.  
- refactor(client): drop the bank, identity and logout methods from both adapters  
    Only the stock memory used them: BankContents, BankUsable,  
    BankKindOfBag, MoveInFlight, ReadsBank, IsBankOpen, StartStock (and  
    its bank and logout events), ClientItemCounts, CharacterIdentity and  
    ShowError are gone from the Classic and the WoW Forever adapter alike.  
    BagContents now returns the carried items only (bags 0-5 on WoW  
    Forever, so the reagent bag counts; 0-4 on the other clients).  
    IsSelfFoundCharacter (the Self-Found rule for Syndicator stock), Now  
    (the trainer memory) and RunStockDiagnostic (the bags lines) stay.  
    The boundary test keeps container, bank and realm calls inside the  
    adapter, checks that BAG\_UPDATE has its one handler in Init, and now  
    also that only the stock scanner reads Syndicator.API.  
- Merge branch 'fix/path-own-crafts'  
- fix(pathfinder): use what the path makes before buying it again  
    A path whose early run makes an item that a later run uses (Bolts of  
    Linen Cloth in Tailoring) put that item on the shopping list again and  
    also counted those crafts as sold, so "You spend" and "Reagents to buy"  
    were too high.  
    The shopping list and the stages now take the steps in path order: a  
    reagent an earlier run made is taken from those crafts first, before  
    any owned stock, and only the rest is needed. Crafts used that way are  
    not counted as sold. An opened run on the Path tab says how many of its  
    crafts go into later runs. The comparison of candidate routes uses the  
    same totals; the step ranking is unchanged.  
    On the bundled Forever data, Tailoring 1-150 no longer buys the 26  
    Bolts of Linen Cloth it makes itself, and its spend falls by about 5%.

# LazyProf

## [v0.10.1](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/tree/v0.10.1) (2026-11-22)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/compare/v0.10.0...v0.10.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/kaldown/LazyProf/releases)

- docs: release v0.10.1  
- docs: describe the Forever data for all nine professions  
- test: cover a recipe learned above its yellow threshold  
    On WoW Forever a few recipes are learned after their yellow threshold (for example Smelt Tin: learned at 65, yellow 50). Checks the skill colour, the skill-up chance and the stage text for such a recipe.

- fix(pricing): only trust same-day auction prices after visiting the auction house  
    Auctionator counts whole days, so a scan from this morning still counted  
    as fresh and beat newer TSM data in the evening. A same-day price now wins  
    only once the auction house was visited since login or /reload. Closing  
    the auction house now expires the cached prices instead of dropping them,  
    so the Planning window's shopping list and the price reports keep the  
    prices their path was calculated with.  
- feat(pricing): use fresh auction prices right after closing the auction house  
    Closing the auction house drops the cached prices and recalculates the  
    path when the profession window is open, so a scan made there is used at  
    once instead of after the 5-minute price cache runs out.  
- feat(pricing): prefer prices from an auction scan made today  
    A reagent or recipe price that Auctionator saw today is now used before  
    TSM. TSM's prices are a snapshot that only reaches the game at login or  
    /reload, so a full scan made just before planning is the newer picture of  
    what the auction house costs. Vendor prices still come first, and older  
    Auctionator prices keep the configured order.  
- fix(pricing): say an auction addon is needed for unpriced reagents  
- fix(client): report learned recipes below their orange level  
    The Forever data check now counts a learned recipe whose skill is below  
    the data's orange level as a difference (that level is too high), says  
    why the check is skipped for another player's, guild or NPC list, and  
    reads the skill the same way the rest of the adapter does.  
- fix(pricing): tell missing prices apart and report the prices used  
    A reagent without a price now says why: its item data is still loading  
    (it fills in by itself), or it has no auction price and no vendor sell  
    value, or the sell estimate is turned off (an auction scan is needed).  
    Before, all of these said "no price yet", even when none would come.  
    The tooltips and /lp diag prices now show the prices the last calculation  
    used instead of reading new ones on hover, so they match the path's  
    totals. The /lp diag prices hint appears only for problems you can fix,  
    and a failing price source no longer stops the whole report.  
- docs: describe the price and recipe data diagnostics  
- feat(client): check recipe data against the Forever client  
    /lp diag forever now compares the recipe data for the open profession with  
    what the client reports for each recipe: the difficulty at the current  
    skill (learned recipes), the gray level, the reagents and the crafted  
    item. Each line counts agreements and differences and lists a sample of  
    the recipes that differ.  
    The diagnostic also says when the profession window is closed, and no  
    longer reports every client recipe as missing from the data when no  
    profession is open.  
- feat(pricing): show where each reagent price comes from  
    Every price now records its source: a vendor price and the addon that  
    recorded it, the TSM value that answered (DBRecent, DBMarket, ...),  
    Auctionator with the number of days since it last saw the item, the  
    vendor sell estimate, or no price yet.  
    The arrow tooltip lists where the path's prices came from and warns when  
    some reagents have no price yet, when Auctionator prices are 3 or more  
    days old, or when reagents only have the sell estimate. This replaces the  
    old "prices may be stale" line, which showed on every path because the  
    scan time it read was never recorded. The shopping list tooltip shows  
    each item's price and source, and /lp diag prices lists every reagent  
    price of the path with what each source says, flagging sources that  
    disagree and stale prices.
